title: Work out an expression
prompt: tokens is an expression written with each operator after its two numbers, such as ["2", "3", "+"] for 2 + 3. The operators are +, - and *. Return the result. For "-", the number that was pushed first is on the left: ["9", "4", "-"] is 9 - 4.
hints: What should happen when the token is a number, and what when it is an operator?
Push numbers. On an operator, pop two numbers, combine them, and push the result.
The first pop gives the right-hand number and the second pop gives the left-hand one.
checkLabels: A single number is its own result.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Uses the two popped numbers in the wrong order for subtraction.
Takes the two oldest numbers instead of the two newest.

feedback: Write the stack out by hand after each token of the long check. An operator always uses the two newest numbers.
